context: a letter from J. N. Hegt, which you are answering
exchanges:
In answer to your kind letter of 28th Novbr. I have the honour to inform you; that we bred this year two Pavo spicifer, which I suppose are male & female.— Neither one of them has got any Sign of spur as yet. They are quite healthy and of the same size as a young Pavo cristatus, and two Pavo cristatus var: alba, all from the same Nest. The eggs were hatched by a Turkey.— They are now six months old. If in Spring there should be a difference in the Size of the spurs between the two species, I will let you know.—

With highest esteem I have the honour to be: | Your’s obediently | J. Noordhoek Hegt | Dir adj.

I thank you for yr letter of Dec 11th & for your great kindness in informing me about the development of the spurs in the 2 species of Pavo. If in the course of the winter or spring you shd perceive any difference in their rate of development, I shd esteem it a singular favour if you wd inform me, as I have no other means of ascertaining the point.

With sincere thanks & respect | I remain dear Sir | yours faithfully | Charles Darwin
